Implements
[programming spec 0007](../../specs/features/002-programming/specs/0007-manual-programming.md).
Source and executable tests are canonical after implementation.

## Scope Of This Plan

This plan gives the owner screens for spec 0006's reservations, which the UI
calls **specials**: build one from media items, a collection block, or a
collection from the beginning; preview it; save it, which publishes it; edit or
cancel it before it starts; and end it early once it airs. It adds
interruption ([ADR 0015](../../adrs/0015-scheduled-interruption.md)): a special
may cut the airing item at its start, now or later, and the channel stream
worker crosses into it seamlessly. There are no drafts.

cuts and ending early; [ADR 0009](../../adrs/0009-programming-blocks.md)'s
2026-10-16 amendment governs regeneration after a reservation write;
[ADR 0014](../../adrs/0014-planned-filler-coverage.md) governs filler and the
schedule revision; [ADR 0008](../../adrs/0008-shared-active-channel-stream-workers.md)
keeps one shared signal through a cut;

**Playout cursor**, **Schedule revision**, **Regeneration boundary**,

### Design Decisions This Plan Makes

The spec leaves these to implementation; each ticket below follows them.
Change them here before the ticket lands, not inside it.

| Decision           | Choice                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| UI name            | The owner sees **Specials**; code and docs say reservation. MAN-008 adds the label to the glossary's **Reservation** row, as **Catalog removal** records its **Delete** label.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Cut rule           | An entry that crosses a reservation's start or end is clipped there. Generation never produces such a crossing, so one exists only when the owner chose it: an interrupting reservation starting inside the airing item, or a running reservation ended inside its own airing program. Cuts are derived in kraziBrain from entries and reservations in the same snapshot, never stored.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Interrupting flag  | `reservations.interrupts` (SQLite boolean, migration `028`). Only a flagged reservation may start before the airing item ends; a save stores the flag only when the start does fall inside the airing item, so a stored flag always means it cut what aired, and it is kept after it starts so the guide can say it cut in.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Start now          | `startsAt` accepts the literal `"now"`, resolved to the server clock inside the write transaction, so browser clock skew never places a cut. `"now"` requires `interrupts: true` when something is airing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Cut reads          | Every server read that finds what airs at an instant goes through `playout-reads.ts`: kraziBrain's `findAiringAt` (cut, playable or not) for the coordinator and interruption, and `findAiringItem` for the regeneration boundary, which also reports nothing airing at an instant a reservation starts and ends airing filler at an interrupting start inside it. Reads list every reservation ending after their earliest loaded entry. The raw SQL covering finders are gone.                                                                                                             |
| Withdrawn cuts     | Regeneration first deletes a withdrawn cut's entries (a reservation block's future entries whose reservation is gone or now starts later), then any entry starting after now but before the boundary. A write replacing a reservation reads what airs without its range or entries. ADR 0014's airing-filler guards allow a filler end to move only to or from an interrupting reservation's start. Deleting a started special stays allowed (spec 0006); a cut that already aired is written into the entry first (ADR 0015 amendment).                                                     |
| Let it finish      | No server change: the browser resubmits with `startsAt` set to the `airingEndsAt` that `reservation_crosses_airing` already returns, without the flag.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Worker notice      | `ChannelStreamManagerContract.scheduleChanged(channelId)`. The server calls it after every committed reservation write. The worker wakes, calls `getCurrent(now)`, and when the same program now ends at another instant no later than the end its FFmpeg process was started for (a cut, or a withdrawn one), adopts that end and discards a preparation made for the old one. When something else already airs, including a filler whose end moved, the cut passed and the worker recovers at once at its offset. Any other change is left to the existing stale handling at the boundary. |
| End early          | `POST /api/channels/:id/reservations/:reservationId/end` with `{ "endsAt": <instant> }` or `{ "after": "airing" }`. The instant must be from now through the current end. `"after": "airing"` ends it when the airing program ends, or now during filler inside it. Writes `end_kind = "explicit"` and regenerates like any reservation write.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Stale preview      | The save body carries `expectedScheduleRevision` from the preview. A mismatch inside the write transaction returns 409 `preview_stale` and writes nothing. A listed-item special's selection is fixed by its saved IDs, so the revision guards only the surrounding schedule.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Retries            | The save body carries a browser-generated `requestKey`, stored in a unique nullable `reservations.request_key`. A repeat returns the saved reservation with 200 and regenerates nothing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| How far ahead      | `startsAt` at most 365 days after now on the server clock; later is `reservation_too_far`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Horizon labels     | The preview reports `beyondHorizon` when the special starts after the channel's coverage, and marks collection programs `estimated: true` then. Nothing is displaced beyond the horizon, so the displaced list is empty.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| From the beginning | The preview accepts the source `{ kind: "collection_from_beginning", mediaCollectionId, playbackMode }` with an ordered mode only; random is refused. It resolves the ordered view into `mediaItemIds`, refuses with `reservation_media_unplayable` naming unavailable members, and returns the list. The browser saves that list as an ordinary `media_items` source.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

**Sequencing note**: MAN-001, MAN-002, MAN-005, MAN-006, and MAN-007 can start
at once. MAN-003 needs MAN-001 and MAN-002. MAN-004 needs MAN-003. MAN-008 needs
MAN-005, MAN-006, and MAN-007, so non-interrupting specials ship without the
cut. MAN-009 needs MAN-003, MAN-004, and MAN-008. MAN-010 needs every other
ticket.

### MAN-001: Workers cross early when the airing item's end moves

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-16. `ChannelStreamManagerContract.scheduleChanged`
forwards a notice to the channel's worker (a starting worker hears it once
ready); the transition loop's boundary waits re-read current and adopt a moved
end, recover at once when the cut already passed, and keep a withdrawn cut on
the running FFmpeg process. `integration/cut.test.ts` proves a mid-media cut on
one session with the viewer attached; it found a corrupt spliced frame, fixed by
holding open PES packets in `mpeg-ts-packet-forwarder.ts`. Follow-up: every
commit, ordinary or cut, pauses delivery about 1.7 s while the next FFmpeg
process starts, because a preparation starts no process before commit.

**Goal**: A running channel stream worker, told the schedule changed, crosses
into the next item at the airing item's new, earlier end on the same signal
session, keeping its subscribers.

**Scope**:

- `ChannelStreamManagerContract.scheduleChanged(channelId)`; a no-op without a
  running worker.
- The transition loop's sleep wakes on the notice; it re-reads current and,
  when the airing cursor is unchanged and its end is earlier, adopts the new
  end, discards any preparation for the old boundary, and prepares again. An
  end already past crosses at once through the existing recovery path, joining
  the next item at its offset.
- `packages/signal/integration/cut.test.ts` under `test:ffmpeg`: a program cut
  mid-media into the next item on one session, with continuous MPEG-TS output
  and the subscriber still attached.

**Out of scope**: Where cuts come from (MAN-002, MAN-003); stopping the worker.

**Blocking dependencies**: None; ADR 0015 is accepted.

**Implementation notes**:

- Owner: media-engineer. Write the worker tests first (tdd skill).
- No packaging change is expected: `commit()` already truncates the previous
  item. If the real-FFmpeg suite shows a gap or broken continuity at a
  mid-media cut, fix it in `ffmpeg-signal-session.ts` and record why here.
- Move an airing item's end through `fake-playout-provider.ts`; check the
  fake still matches the real provider's contract (test-double fidelity).
- Keep the loop reading as its transitions; a wake is one more reason the
  sleep ends, not a second loop.

**Verification**: Worker tests prove a notice with an earlier end commits the
next item at the new end; a notice with no change leaves the boundary; a
preparation made for the old boundary is discarded, never committed; a past end
crosses at once. `npm run test:ffmpeg` (signal) proves the cut. Run the full
check list.

**Docs impact**: None.

### MAN-002: kraziBrain derives cuts

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-16. `playout/cuts.ts` clips an entry at any reservation
start or end inside its airtime, applied first by `deriveChannelState`,
`selectFollowingPlayout`, `buildPlayoutTimeline`, and `listPlannedFiller`;
`cuts.test.ts` covers each verification case. Decisions: kraziBrain's
`Reservation` gains no `interrupts` field, because the cut rule needs only
boundaries and nothing in kraziBrain would read it; the flag lives on the
server's reservation row (MAN-003). `findRegenerationBoundary` already takes
the airing item as given, so the server's `findAiringItem` and started-turn
lookup become cut-aware in MAN-003, whose reads must also pass every
reservation whose boundary falls inside a loaded entry, not only those ending
after the read instant.

**Goal**: kraziBrain clips an entry at a reservation boundary it crosses, and
every playout answer uses the clipped entries.

**Scope**:

- One cut function in `packages/krazi-brain/src/playout/`, applied before
  filler derivation, `deriveChannelState`, `selectFollowingPlayout`, and
  `buildPlayoutTimeline`.
- `findRegenerationBoundary` and the started-turn lookup see the airing
  item's cut end.
- `Reservation` gains `interrupts`.

**Out of scope**: Persistence, routes, the worker notice.

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Implementation notes**:

- Owner: backend-engineer. Write the tests first (tdd skill).
- A cut entry's progress is unchanged: it started airing, so it counts as
  aired (spec 0007's progress table).

**Verification**: Tests prove an entry crossing an interrupting reservation's
start ends there and the special follows with no gap or filler; an entry
crossing a reservation's moved end ends there and ordinary programming
follows; channel state during the special never reports the cut entry; join
offsets inside a cut entry are unchanged before the cut; removing the
reservation restores the entry's full airtime. Run the full check list.

**Docs impact**: None.

### MAN-003: Interrupting specials cut the airing item

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-17. Migration `028` adds `reservations.interrupts`; create,
PATCH, and preview take `interrupts` and `startsAt: "now"`; every committed
write notifies `ChannelRuntime.scheduleChanged`, logging a failure. All reads of
what airs go through the cut (see the Cut reads and Withdrawn cuts rows), and
the guide and XMLTV show the cut end. `reservations/interruption.test.ts`
covers the routes, catalog removal, and withdrawn and aired cuts,
`channel-stream-acceptance.test.ts` the live cut on a
scripted packager (whose preparations now commit), and the server
`test:ffmpeg` "real FFmpeg cut" a later cut and a cut now within a second.

**Goal**: The owner can save a special that starts inside the airing item, now
or later, and the live channel cuts into it within the exact-start tolerance
without disconnecting viewers.

**Scope**:

- Migration `028` adds `reservations.interrupts`; one schema change.
- The create and preview bodies accept `interrupts` and `startsAt: "now"`; a
  flagged reservation may start from now until the airing item ends; an
  unflagged one is still refused with `reservation_crosses_airing`.
- Every server read that finds entries by instant applies the MAN-002 cut:
  `playout/playout-reads.ts`, the schedule window, XMLTV, the transition
  coordinator, and `findAiringItem`.
- `ChannelRuntime` picks `scheduleChanged`; every committed reservation write
  calls it after commit, and a failure is logged without undoing the commit.
- Editing or deleting an interrupting special before its start restores the
  airing item and notifies the worker the same way.

**Out of scope**: Ending a running special (MAN-004); the browser (MAN-009).

**Blocking dependencies**: MAN-001, MAN-002.

**Implementation notes**:

- Owner: backend-engineer, with media-engineer for the server `test:ffmpeg`
  case.
- Search for every query that selects entries covering an instant before
  changing any; route them through the shared reads instead of adding cut
  logic to each.
- An interrupted airing filler ends at the special's start; ADR 0014's
  `airing_filler_conflict` stays for unflagged writes.

**Verification**: Route tests prove a flagged special inside the airing item
saves and an unflagged one is refused; `"now"` uses the server clock; the guide
and XMLTV show the cut end; the coordinator refuses a preparation made before
the cut. A server test with the scripted packager proves the worker commits
the special at the cut after the notice. `npm run test:ffmpeg` (server) proves
a later cut and a cut now each land within 1 second with the subscriber
attached. Run the full check list.

**Docs impact**: None.

### MAN-004: End a running special early

**Goal**: The owner can end a running special, letting the airing program
finish or cutting it at a chosen instant, and normal programming follows.

**Scope**:

- `POST /api/channels/:id/reservations/:reservationId/end` with `endsAt` or
  `"after": "airing"`, per the decisions table; other edits to a started
  reservation keep `reservation_started`.
- The write regenerates from the new end, advances the revision once, and
  notifies the worker.

**Out of scope**: Editing a running special's programs.

**Blocking dependencies**: MAN-003.

**Implementation notes**: Owner: backend-engineer. The MAN-002 cut rule
already clips the special's own airing program at its new end; add no second
rule.

**Verification**: Route tests prove `"after": "airing"` ends at the airing
program's end; an instant inside it cuts there; an instant before now or after
the current end is refused; a not-yet-started special is refused with a
message pointing at edit or cancel; normal programming follows from the new
end; a cut lands within 1 second in the server `test:ffmpeg` suite. Run the
full check list.

**Docs impact**: None.

### MAN-005: Saving guards against stale previews, retries, and far dates

**Goal**: A save publishes exactly what was previewed, at most once, and never
more than a year ahead.

**Scope**:

- Create and PATCH require `expectedScheduleRevision`; a mismatch returns 409
  `preview_stale`.
- Create takes `requestKey`, stored in unique `reservations.request_key`
  (migration `029`, or `028` if MAN-003 has not landed); a repeat returns the
  saved reservation and regenerates nothing.
- `reservation_too_far` beyond 365 days, in preview and save.

**Out of scope**: The browser (MAN-008).

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Implementation notes**: Owner: backend-engineer. Follow
`programming-rebuild-routes.ts` for the key; reuse `racing-schedule.ts` for
the concurrent-retry test.

**Verification**: Route tests prove a save after an unrelated assignment edit
is refused and writes nothing; two concurrent saves with one key create one
reservation and advance the revision once; a start 366 days out is refused.
Run the full check list.

**Docs impact**: None.

### MAN-007: Preview a collection from the beginning

**Goal**: The owner can turn a collection in an ordered mode into a fixed list
of every member, first to last, and see unavailable members before saving.

**Scope**:

- The preview accepts the `collection_from_beginning` source and returns the
  resolved `mediaItemIds` with the usual preview; random is refused as an
  invalid request; unavailable members refuse with
  `reservation_media_unplayable`.
- The save body does not accept this source; the browser saves the returned
  list.

**Out of scope**: Collection progress and marathon cooldown, which a listed
special never touches already.

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Implementation notes**: Owner: backend-engineer. Reuse `orderMembers` and
`describeOrderedView`; do not write a second ordering.

**Verification**: Route tests prove an eight-film collection in release order
resolves to all eight, first film first, with a program-derived end; a
collection with an unavailable member is refused naming it; random is
refused. Run the full check list.

**Docs impact**: None.

### MAN-008: Specials in My Channels

**Goal**: The owner can list, build, preview, save, edit, and cancel
specials that do not interrupt anything.

**Scope**:

- A Specials section in the channel editor listing the channel's reservations
  with start, end, and what airs.
- An editor for a media-item list, a collection block with an explicit end,
  or a collection from the beginning; start up to a year ahead.

**Out of scope**: The **What is airing now** choice and ending early (MAN-009).

  make it serve more than one capability, regroup the whole folder in this
  change and drop the exception, per AGENTS.md.
- Glossary: add the **Specials** UI label to **Reservation**.

**Verification**: jsdom tests prove each source previews and saves; a stale
preview asks for a refresh; a far start is refused; edit and cancel work
before the start; a removal refusal links to the special. Run the full check
list.

**Docs impact**: Glossary label.

### MAN-009: The What is airing now choice and ending early

**Goal**: The owner can start a special while something airs, after it or by
cutting it, and end a running special early the same two ways.

**Scope**:

- When a special's start falls before the airing item ends, the editor asks
  **What is airing now**: **Let it finish** (resubmit at `airingEndsAt`) or
  **Stop it at the special's start** (`interrupts`), with a **Start now**
  shortcut, worded like `rebuild-dialog.tsx`.
- A running special shows **End early** with **Let it finish** and **Stop it
  at** a chosen time or now.

**Out of scope**: Changing the existing rebuild and removal interruptions.

**Blocking dependencies**: MAN-003, MAN-004, MAN-008.

**Implementation notes**: Owner: backend-engineer for web work. The choice
never appears when the start is after the airing item ends.

**Verification**: jsdom tests prove the choice appears only on overlap; each
option sends the right request; end-early sends `"after": "airing"` or the
chosen instant. Run the full check list.

**Docs impact**: None.

### MAN-010: Accept the spec's whole acceptance list end to end

**Goal**: One acceptance suite proves every spec 0007 criterion, plus spec
0004's full-series criterion that waited on this spec.

**Scope**:

- `apps/server/src/reservations/manual-programming-acceptance.test.ts` drives
  specials through the API beside assignments and rules, across a cut, an
  early end, a restart, and chunked coverage.
- Map each criterion to a passing test in this ticket's Status block; the
  full-series test also proves spec 0004's criterion.

**Out of scope**: New behavior.

**Blocking dependencies**: MAN-001 through MAN-009.

**Implementation notes**: Reuse the fixtures above; add no new doubles. An
in-scope criterion already proven by an earlier ticket's test may cite it.

**Verification**: Every criterion maps to a passing test; full check list plus
`npm run test:ffmpeg`.

**Docs impact**: Spec 0007 `Status:` becomes `Implemented`. Spec 0004 becomes
`Implemented`. Spec 0006 becomes `Implemented`.
